messages.author: 3afa2b67ef806635
messages.subject: Equivalent to strip.white in readr
parts:
Hi All,

When using read.csv (etc.) to read a comma- or tab-delimited file that contains character data, I commonly use strip.white=TRUE and na.chars="" (two quotes with nothing between them). That way if someone uses two consecutive delimiters, or any number of blanks between the delimiters, I'll get NAs before I convert the character vector to a factor. Using read_csv or read_tsv I can specify na=" " (single blank) and use a single blank in the data between delimiters, and I'll get the desired NAs. However, in that case two delimiters in a row, or two or more blanks will not generate NAs. I can use a conditional assignment after the fact to set NAs, but is there a way to generate NAs from zero or >=2 blanks in read_csv or read_tsv?

Thanks,
Bob

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Equivalent to strip.white in readr
parts:
Not yet, but it's a frequently requested feature so is likely to be in
the next version.
Hadley
